note: The two sets are nearly identical; B is A plus one additional claim (chord 5.7 m at r/R = 0.25), which matches the chord curve just past its ~5.8 m maximum and is therefore a correct, useful data point that A omits. Both sets otherwise share the same strengths (root/tip twist, prebend, pitch-axis and thickness readings broadly consistent with the curves) and the same defects: contradictory readings at the same span station (twist 14/15/15.5 deg at r/R = 0, relative thickness 95/100 % at r/R = 0, chord 1.5/0.5 m at r/R = 1.0) and four claims repeated verbatim. Because B adds a supported claim and loses nothing, it is marginally better.
remarks: Page is five x-y plots only, so every value must be read off a curve; precision is limited and borderline readings (chord 5.2 m at r/R = 0.2 where the curve peaks near 5.8 m, relative thickness 40 % at r/R = 0.25 where the curve is near 35 %) were not scored as wrong. Both sets state mutually exclusive values at the same station (twist 14/15/15.5 deg at r/R = 0; relative thickness 95/100 % at r/R = 0; chord 1.5/0.5 m at r/R = 1.0) and repeat four claims (prebend 0 m at 0.0, prebend -4 m at 1.0, relative thickness 100 % at 0.0, twist -2 deg at 0.85). Most quotes are axis labels or panel captions (e.g. '(c) Twist') that do not contain the claimed number, and the relative-thickness 22 % claim quotes the tick label '20', so quote support is weak throughout. Both sets also leave obvious curve endpoints unstated (e.g. chord ~5.2 m at r/R = 0, relative thickness ~22 % at the tip).
